claims.title: Setup regex over-matches and misclassifies run time
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Setup regex over-matches and misclassifies run time**

SETUP_RE is an unanchored alternation: `checkout|setup|cache|install` matches anywhere in a step name, so steps like "Run npm run setup-db", "Run cache-busting test" or "Run install-check" are counted as setup time rather than run time. The medians in the cookbook's symptom table ("setup over half of job time") can therefore be skewed. Consider anchoring to `^(Run )?actions/(checkout|setup-|cache)` or known install commands.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|skills/working-with-github-actions/scripts/ci-audit.sh|6f0843c7c27b24f9.1 -->

claims.title: Setup regex over-matches step names, skewing setup/run split
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Setup regex over-matches step names, skewing setup/run split**

SETUP_RE is an unanchored substring match (case-insensitive) for `checkout|setup|cache|install`. Any step whose name contains these words (e.g. "Run install-check tests", "Setup test database", "Test cache invalidation") is counted as setup, not run time. This can misattribute real work to setup and push users toward the wrong lever (e.g. the cookbook's "setup over half of job time" row). Consider documenting this caveat or tightening the pattern.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|skills/working-with-github-actions/scripts/ci-audit.sh|6f0843c7c27b24f9.1 -->

claims.title: API errors are silently swallowed, producing misleading audit results
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**API errors are silently swallowed, producing misleading audit results**

`gh api ... 2>/dev/null || true` hides every failure (rate limiting, 403, network errors). A run whose jobs cannot be fetched is dropped from the medians without any notice. The header still reports `runs: N`, and `n=` per job shrinks silently, so the audit can show skewed numbers with no sign that data is missing. Stderr should be surfaced, or failures counted and reported (e.g. 'warning: failed to fetch jobs for run $id').

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
    gh api "repos/$repo/actions/runs/$id/jobs" --jq '.jobs[]' || echo "warning: could not fetch jobs for run $id in $repo" >&2
```

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|skills/working-with-github-actions/scripts/ci-audit.sh|1da08cbfefc74012.0 -->
<!-- ai-review:sfp=4ed8e0d0a7d01a59 -->

claims.title: Even-sized samples report upper middle value as median
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Even-sized samples report upper middle value as median**

`sort | .[length/2|floor]` returns the upper-middle element for even-length arrays rather than the average of the two middle values. With default 15 runs this is fine for odd counts, but jobs with an even n (e.g. after skips or failures) get a biased median. The same `med` is used for wall-clock and per-step medians.

claims.title: Jobs endpoint is not paginated and errors are swallowed
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Jobs endpoint is not paginated and errors are swallowed**

`gh api` on the jobs endpoint returns only the first 30 jobs by default, so matrix runs with more jobs are silently truncated. Also `2>/dev/null || true` hides request failures so incomplete data is reported as a successful audit.

claims.title: `gh api repos/$repo/actions/runs/$id/jobs` returns at most 30 jobs by default, so large matrix runs are truncated. Failures are also swallowed by `2>/dev/null || true`. claims.title: Setup regex over-matches step names and jobs from different workflows are merged
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Setup regex over-matches step names and jobs from different workflows are merged**

SETUP_RE contains unanchored `setup|cache|install|checkout`, so a test step like "Test cache" or "Run install tests" counts as setup and is subtracted from run time, skewing the setup-vs-run split that the cookbook uses to choose levers. Also, `group_by(.job)` merges same-named jobs across workflows in the default all-workflows mode, mixing unrelated measurements. Anchor the regex to known action/step prefixes and group by workflow plus job (e.g. via the run's workflow name).

claims.title: Skipped-filter job can leave a required check green
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Skipped-filter job can leave a required check green**

If the `changes` job fails, the dependent `docs` job is skipped, and a skipped job counts as success for branch protection. A broken filter can therefore pass the required check. Add a final always-run gate job that fails when `needs.changes.result != 'success'`. Also add `pull-requests: read` permissions, and `fetch-depth: 0` for push events.

claims.title: If `changes` fails, `docs` (which needs it) is skipped, and a skipped job reports success to branch protection. A broken filter can then let the required docs check go green without evaluating anything. The recipe also lacks `pull-requests: read` permission and `fetch-depth` for push events, which are the likely causes of a filter failure. Recommend an always-running gate job that fails when `changes` fails (`if: always()` and check `needs.changes.result`), and note the permissions.

claims.title: Failed jobs fetch is not detected when gh fails inside a pipe
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Failed jobs fetch is not detected when gh fails inside a pipe**

`gh api ... | jq -c ... || { warning }` only reports failure of the last pipeline command (`jq`), unless `pipefail` applies. With `set -euo pipefail` the pipeline status is nonzero if `gh` fails, so the warning fires, but any partial output from a paginated fetch that failed midway has already been streamed to the aggregator. The run is then included with only some of its jobs, even though the warning says it was 'excluded from medians'. Buffer the fetch result first, and only emit it on success.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|skills/working-with-github-actions/scripts/ci-audit.sh|79bcfc7725425c0c.0 -->

claims.title: Pipeline masks gh api failures; failed fetch may still emit partial output
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Pipeline masks gh api failures; failed fetch may still emit partial output**

The `gh api ... | jq -c ... || { warning }` construct only catches the failure of the last pipeline command (`jq`). Without `pipefail` scoped here, it relies on the global `set -o pipefail` (stated in the PR). With it, a failed `gh api --paginate` after emitting some pages could output partial jobs for that run and also print the warning, so the run is described as 'excluded' while some of its jobs are still counted. This is a minor inaccuracy in the warning message and a bounded skew in medians.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|skills/working-with-github-actions/scripts/ci-audit.sh|79bcfc7725425c0c.0 -->

claims.title: Pipeline masks gh api failures in job fetch loop
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Pipeline masks gh api failures in job fetch loop**

In `gh api ... | jq -c ... || { warning }`, the `||` applies only to the last pipeline command (`jq`) because `pipefail` is not applied per-command here. With `set -o pipefail` the pipeline status becomes non-zero if `gh api` fails, so the warning does fire. However, the `--paginate --jq '.jobs[]'` output from a failed partial page may already have been emitted to the downstream jq before the failure, so a run with partial jobs is still included in the medians despite the warning saying it is excluded.

The `gh api ... | jq -c ... || { warning }` construct works per-iteration, but if `gh api --paginate` fails partway after emitting some pages, partial job records for that run are still emitted to the aggregate while the warning claims the run was "excluded from medians". The warning text is therefore inaccurate for partial failures, and medians include partial data for that run.

claims.title: Process-substitution while loop pipes into jq without pipefail visibility for gh failures
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Process-substitution while loop pipes into jq without pipefail visibility for gh failures**

`gh api --paginate ... | jq -c ... || { warning }` only reports a warning when the last command in the pipeline (jq) fails. With `set -o pipefail` the pipeline status does include gh failures, so that case is covered. However, `jq -c '. + {wf:$wf}'` with `--paginate --jq '.jobs[]'` is fine. The remaining issue is that a partial failure mid-pagination can emit some jobs from that run before failing, and the warning then claims the run is 'excluded from medians' even though its already-emitted jobs are included. The message is inaccurate and the data is partially included.

**Per-SHA concurrency group is placed in the wrong ternary position for non-main refs**

The documented concurrency group uses `format('{0}-{1}', github.workflow, github.ref)` for non-main refs. claims.title: Cancelled jobs skew medians
claims.text:
🟡 **P2**

**Cancelled jobs skew medians**

Only `skipped` jobs are excluded. Cancelled jobs (common with cancel-in-progress, which the cookbook recommends) have truncated durations and pull queue/run/total medians down, understating real CI time.

*Suggested fix:*

```suggestion
    map(select(.started_at and .completed_at and .conclusion != "skipped" and .conclusion != "cancelled")
```

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|skills/working-with-github-actions/scripts/ci-audit.sh|d29f935d40ad4950.0 -->
<!-- ai-review:sfp=4ac0edfac10d0793 -->

claims.title: Setup regex counts test steps named like setup keywords
claims.text:
🟢 **P3**

**Setup regex counts test steps named like setup keywords**

The unanchored alternatives `cache`, `install`, `restore` and `set ?up` after `^` only match at the start, but names like `Cache tests` or `Install smoke test` would still be counted as setup and subtracted from run time. The cookbook uses the setup/run ratio to choose levers, so misclassification can mislead; the limitation should be documented in the header.

<!-- ai-review:fp=bug|skills/working-with-github-actions/scripts/ci-audit.sh|81ad55f83c577a38.1 -->
